title: AES-CTR counter increment assumes big-endian; hardware endianness unverified
description: After hardware AES-CTR, crypto2dev_port.c manually increments aes->reg as a big-endian byte array (rightmost byte first). wolfSSL's software AES-CTR counter increment uses IncrementAesCounter which on some builds increments a 32-bit word in host byte order. If the hardware uses a different counter representation, aes->reg goes out of sync with the hardware counter after the first call, producing wrong output on the second and subsequent calls. Trigger: any multi-call AES-CTR stream where the hardware uses little-endian counter increment and the host is little-endian. No test exercises multi-call CTR. Fix: document the assumed counter endianness and add a multi-call CTR KAT to verify the counter tracks correctly.
